name: Krasnodar Krai-Crimea Gas Pipeline (Kuban-Crimea)

values.OtherEnglishNames: Kuban-Crimea Gas Pipeline, Kuban-Crimea Main Gas Pipeline

researcher_notes: Not in GGIT (checked 20260930 snapshot for Crimea/Kerch/Simferopol/Sevastopol/Kuban: no row; P1470/P5551 = Krasnodar-Serpukhov, different corridor; P2425/P2426 end at Anapa). Operating: commissioned 27 Dec 2016 (neftegaz, video launch by Putin), scheduled mode by early 2017. Length 358.7 km is the operator-announced figure incl. 2-string Tuzla/Kerch Strait crossing and 27.3 km Simferopol branch (neftegaz 211685 + energyland, two independent publishers; Kommersant: 16 km subsea + 341 km Kerch-Sevastopol on Crimea side). Other figures: ~314 km (2016 Glavgosexpertiza design, stroygaz/aif), ~400 km (ru.wikipedia, krymr, yugsn) -- design/rounded; 358.7 chosen as post-commissioning. Segment boundary vs anapa-taman: Kuban-Crimea is its own line; official 2015 route description (neftegaz 139571) puts only ~1.2 km on the Taman peninsula before two ~16 km Kerch Strait strings (+~20.4 km Kerch peninsula land), so the mainland-Russia portion is ~1 km and does NOT overlap the 106 km Anapa-Taman Southern Corridor trunk; the line ties into the Southern Corridor (ru.wikipedia: between Kazachya and Russkaya CS; not independently verified here, and ru.wikipedia's 137.5 km 'Krasnodar Krai-Kerch' first-stage figure conflicts with the 1.2 km official figure -- unresolved, flag for route work). Crimea-internal legs (Kerch-Simferopol-Sevastopol, ~341 km) are part of one commissioned project with the Kerch Strait crossing, so staged as ONE Russia-Ukraine cross-border row (start Taman, Russia; end Sevastopol, Ukraine per GEM naming conventions) rather than split off as Ukraine-internal; if reviewers prefer a split, the natural cut is Taman-Kerch Strait (~38 km incl. Kerch landfall) vs Kerch-Simferopol(-branch)-Sevastopol. Capacity: 2.2 bcm/y planned throughput, expandable to 4.4 bcm/y (neftegaz); design/nameplate often cited as 4-4.4. Diameter: 700 mm main line, two 500 mm branches (yugsn; ru.wikipedia agrees, 500 mm Simferopol-Sevastopol). Owner: Chernomorneftegaz is the officially named customer/owner of the project (Crimean state unitary enterprise, nationalized by Russian-installed authorities 2014; krymr, kommersant); builder Stroygazmontazh; Gazprom's role (queue note) not established, so Parent left blank -- entity_lookup: Chernomorneftegaz not in the entity table, new entity. Also noted: vz.ru 2025-08 reports the line now feeds reverse flow to Kherson/Zaporizhzhia. Route: no official GIS found; OSM ~135 km trace is partial; RouteType/RouteAccuracy/RouteNotes left blank for the route-creation workflow (needs Kerch Strait crossing south of the Crimean Bridge, Kerch-Simferopol-Sevastopol).
